metric_rationale: By analyzing the experimental design, we can identify specific trials where Tallying results in a tie (the number of feature wins is equal for both options) but Take The Best has a strict preference based on the highest-validity discriminating cue. Under the Tallying theory, subjects will guess randomly on these trials, resulting in an expected TTB-alignment of 0.5. Under the Take The Best theory, subjects will systematically choose the TTB-favored option, resulting in an expected TTB-alignment significantly higher than 0.5. Measuring the proportion of choices that align with TTB on these specific divergence trials provides a highly targeted and robust way to discriminate between the two models.

Trial 9 is the only trial in the design where the two theories have opposing strict preferences. For A=[0, 1, 0, 1] and B=[0, 0, 1, 0], Tallying counts 2 wins for A (features 1 and 3) and 1 win for B (feature 2), thus strongly preferring A. In contrast, Take The Best consults cues in validity order: feature 0 is a tie, and feature 2 (the next most valid cue) favors B, so TTB strongly prefers B. By measuring the rate at which subjects choose A on this specific trial, we obtain a metric that evaluates to ~1.0 under Tallying and ~0.0 under Take The Best.
